title: CRLA/36/2003 of NOOR HASAN Vs STATE

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT
NAINITAL
Criminal Appeal No.36 of 2003
Noor Hasan
 Ö Appellant
Versus
State of Uttaranchal
 Ö Respondent
Sri T.A. Khan, Senior Advocate for the appellant.
Sri V.K. Gemini, Dy. Adv. General (Criminal) for the State.
Honíble Servesh Kumar Gupta, J.
 Appellant Noor Hasan has been convicted by
the learned Additional Sessions Judge, Udham Singh
Nagar in Sessions Trial No.12 of 2002, for the offence
under section 18 of the Narcotics Drugs & Psychotropic
Substances Act, 1985. He was sentenced to two yearsí
rigorous imprisonment, in addition to fine of
Rs.2,000/-, in default of which, six monthsí additional
rigorous imprisonment was awarded.
2. Appellant Noor Hasan is present in person
before the Court. He appears to be a physically
challenged person and is unable to even walk freely.
3. The allegation against the appellant Noor
Hasan is that on the relevant date, time and place of
occurence, two kilograms of Poppy Straw was recovered
from him.
4. Learned senior counsel has drawn the
attention of this Court towards the variations in
quantity of the amount when it was allegedly recovered,
then sent to the Forensic Science Laboratory and
subsequently received back in the Court, which, by

2
itself, is enough to create a reasonable doubt in the
prosecution story.
5. However, learned senior counsel for the
appellant does not want to argue the appeal on merits
but beseeches the clemency of this Court looking to the
pitiable condition of his client (appellant).
6. Having regard to the entire facts and
circumstances of the case, the Court also feels that
such appellant should be looked into with mercy. It is
pertinent to mention that only two kilograms of Poppy
Straw was allegedly recovered from the appellant which
is much below the commercial quantity. There is no
minimum punishment, or the limit of fine, prescribed
under the provisions of Section 18(c) of the said Act, as
amended on 02.10.2001.
7. The appellant has already been in gaol in this
matter with effect from 17.9.2001 to 8.11.2001, i.e. one
month and 25 days, and after his conviction from the
trial court, since 23.1.2003 to 30.11.2001 i.e. for
almost eight days. So, he has been in detention for
more than two months. That apart, once he was
further kept in caption after issuance of the non-bailable warrants by this Court against him.
8. So, looking to the period of detention of the
appellant, the Court deems it proper to reduce the
sentence of the appellant to two months, which he has
already undergone, instead of two yearsí R.I., as
awarded by the trial court. The fine of Rs.2,000/- is
hereby reduced to Rs.100/- (Rupees one hundred
only), which will be deposited by him before the trial

3
court within a period of one month from today. It is
hereby made clear that in case of failure of depositing
the fine, as reduced by this Court, the appeal shall be
deemed to have been dismissed on the question of
sentence also.
9. Subject to above, the appeal is dismissed on
merits with the modification in the sentence as
recorded above.
10. Let a copy of this judgment along with the
record of the case be transmitted to the court
concerned.
 (Servesh Kumar Gupta, J.)
01.04.2014
Rdang
